review_text: Function hall 1 and 2 usage went well. Place is clean, malamig and the buffet set up was well-prepared. Must order - BEEF KALDERETA and MOLO SOUP. Masarap tlga ang kaldereta. Generous sa serving during the buffet, madami sobra sa food kahit almost 50 pax kame. Definitely recommending Cafe Julieta for family gatherings and the likes. Kudos to all the staff. Very helpful and they really know what they're going. Good Job. Breakfast meals (1 viand) at 395 +7%SC with basic coffee. +50 pesos for brewed. The early AM staff are very nice, respectful and pro-active. Credit card is accepted.
Service is great! Good place to host events. Professional communication and service. Everything went smoothly. Food was also great.
I have not been here since it first opened, and now with regret. Staff, food, and ambience absolutely lovely.

Lunched here as a group years back. And this time for early breakfast (7:30 a.m.). The Filipino/American breakfast was swift but the Continental took much longer. I expected the Hot Chocolate (tableya) to be thicker, tastier and NOT blended with milk and sugar when it reached our table. The breads were a lot as I had all four (4) selection. Four (4) spreads went with the plate as well. If you are a light breakfast eater this would definitely be very filling and would seem too much but will get you through to lunch or even a few hours after. It's imperative to try their chocolate cake in can. A hotel plus pool form part of this place's added attraction. So first-timers, you be the judge.
Clean pool. Food a bit expensive. Restaurant is spotless. They should promote bbq pork events. Huge party time ⏲️ 🙌. We will return

We've been here twice in search of a place to with a decent wifi and an area to have work considering the current situation. They open at 10am, then closes at 2pm; reopens by 4:30pm. We had to find a place to work. The head server was gracious to accomodate as even before 4:30pm and served us even it was his breaktime. Place as they is instagrammble. I looove the interiors. Food is really great. Salmon is cooked just right. Baby back ribs is smoked to perfection. and the Tarragon tea seals the deal. It's less people dining in here due to early curfew (thankfully it has been extended to 9pm now!). But if you have time, this place is perfect for family. They also have take-out. I always hear they have expensive menu. But they also have set meals which is wallet-friendly and still mouth-watering. I attached the menu for your reference. Ample parking space too. Customer service: 5/5 for the head server!! there is one female server though who's too rude but we'd forgive her. To the owners, give the head server a raise! 😊

We have different pros and cons about a place, especially its food. So I'll start with the place. I love the place, because it's cozy and I feel completely comfortable, especially the lights and decorations are cute. The concept fit with place. They have nice and clean comfort rooms, and the pool side is nicely decorated too which is nice. The staffs are friendly, welcoming, nice and accomodating. The food is good, there's nothing extravagant with the taste, but that's okay, except for the Sisig (I forgot the price) and Seafood Laksa (299pesos). It was presentable enough for me. Food is quite pricey but it's good enough for 3-4 persons (unless all of you are voracious eaters). The cons for me is still in the food. The gravy in our Fried Chicken Steak (339pesos) was a bit cold, but the chicken is fresh and warm when served to our table. The Baby Back Ribs w/ Asian BBQ sauce (369pesos) is good and tasty, the meat is not that meaty but I think it's okay. Overall, the place and staffs are okay but there's need to improve in the food. I'll go back here in some other time to try other foods in their menu. I attached some pictures below. I forgot to take a picture for the Baby Back ribs, but there are the others that you might want to see. I also took the menu if you wanted to know how much their food, buffet, function hall and swimming pool cost.

The ambiance is amazing but they should add more to their menu considering that they make tasty food. However, one of my friends dessert bread has molds in it, the order was cancelled but they did not compensate my friend considering that she was able to consume half of the bread before realizing the her food tastes weird. P. S My griled cheese sandwich was too hard for my like, i can definitely throw those to someone and hate and be able to make a small injury on that person. That's how hard their grilled cheese sandwich was.

This place has a cozy ambiance -- well-lighted, great interiors, instagrammable. There are also many delicious dishes available on their menu. No wonder many families and yuppies choose to dine at Cafe Julieta. The only issue I have is that most of their servers are rude...

Total Experience is a twinkling 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 🌟 We celebrated the brother of my sister-in-law's birthday one Sunday lunch time, and took advantage of their PHP 500/pax consumable offer. 🏖 HOW IT WORKS: those who want to take a dip is a good P500. But is consumable in food and drinks. *9 pax went to swim [P4500.00] 👍The place is convenient. If you arw looking for a place to get a dip with great meal, Cafe Julieta is a nice place to go to. They have a kiddie pool and pool for adults that can go as deep as 10ft. Their food is also great at a reasonable price. We had their.. 🍽 asian stir fried noodles 🍽 catfish crablet mango salad *my ultimate fave 😋 🍽 house salad 🍽 ceasar salad 🍽 baby back ribs with asian bbq sauce 🍽 fish and chips *served cream dorry and fries with mayo dip 🍽 honey soy chicken 😋 🍽 beef salpicao All I can say is their food is great. I rarely get to like beef dishes, but their beef is legitimately tender. They also serve beer, liquors, coffee and pastries. The pool side is clean. The shower room they come with is well maintained. We also enjoyed their bossa set playing behind family time. The only recommendable thing I can share is, the resto seemed to be short-staffed. Our attendant is super patient, mind you, we are 13 individuals that were served pretty well. I'd give them a 4 for the "must imprpve on", but I love the vibes of the place, their staff, ammenities and of course, their food. I'd definitely come back and try to checkin and experience their room accommodation. -future feedback to come.
Food was good. Staff was very nice. Too bad they don't have dinner rolls. Steak was good but wasn't cooked to the right temp.

When I'm back home in my country, I always make sure to go to the new restaurants in town. We passed by this so cute restaurant with enough lightings and pretty set up inviting us to come inside. This place is perfect for dinner with friends or family or just a catching up session over a cup of tea and a slice of your favorite cake. Although I would suggest for them to improve the tea cups they are using to match their pretty ambiance. The picture attched is their Caesar salad which I would like to try making at home since I like how simple they made it yet it's so refreshing to eat.

The taragona tea is quite minty regardless ita soothing to the throat. What I love is the sans rival perfect for my taste buds. The manager was so accommodating giving me more information that I needed about the consummables and if how much would be the staycation, entrance and if letting the kids swim the pool...

Yummy empanada. Sinful desserts. Great relaxing ambience. This could be 5 stars but i havent tried the buffet yet. Updated: 20190512 Excellent food choices, cozy ambience, and friendly servers. Perhaps they can a little bit more flexible for off-the-menu requests, like the pomelo salad in the buffet which they didn't allow to be served ala carte, bacause, "that's the policy!" 😢
We went there for our Christmas party. The food was good but the atmosphere was not good for Christmas too plain, no decorations. A regular party would be ok but for Christmas not

A nice café in Juna for rendezvous with friends. There is ample parking space if you come here early prior lunch. I got coffee and house salad (vinegraitte dressing) a good option for vegetarians. I should try other food items on my next visit.
Mix of Western and Filipino food done very competently. Service is rather inattentive, but very polite ... bonus: with a minimum spend per person, you can use the lovely pool.
Delicious food and great service. Chef personally greeted us and served his creation.
a very nice to hangout with friends and family
We came in during weekdays so we had the place for us. Food was great & delish.
Nice Restaurant with a nice swimming pool. Food is enough to crunch your craving.
Nice place. Kiddy pool is shaded. Food is good. Rooms are new. Tempting cakes. Ample parking at the back.
the food is delicious and the servings are big. nice place for simple get together
The place has a good vibe , but the food was ok , staff isn't fast , had to ask to provide extras like water , sauce , food isn't worth the price

Perfect 5/5 I am just a lowkey commoner, all I can say is CASA/CAFE JULIETA IS A BEST PLACE TO CHILL. THE POOL IS ABSOLUTELY GREAT. WATER IS FRESH AND FOOD 100%. Beautiful. Great job Casa/Cafe Julieta
Nice place, food is yummy. Yayamanin the ambience. Clean swimming pool. Big parking space too.

The staff were very welcoming and as soon as we arrived, the manager welcomed us and took as to a table and rearranged it for us to fit in one table. The food was very nice especially their lumpia. The mac and cheese were a bit too much for me but still good for people who have children. Their frappes were also great and not overly sweet. The place itself was very bright and beautiful which makes it a good place to dine into at night. Over all my experience in this cafe was a 4.6/5.
Food tastes great! Customer service is excellent!
Must try their Oreo cheesecake ❤️❤️❤️👌🏻 You have to. 😅 …

The food was okay. The mushroom and truffle pasta was good, but I would have wanted the sauteed seafood to have a bit stronger flavors. But overall it was an okay dining experience. The location is accessible and the wait staff was courteous as well.

Super nice place with a lot of seating capacity. Their service was good. There were delicious food, I think it was the sisig. It was mouth-watering. The chicken of the Tinola was a little bit hard to bite and the crispy noodles were toooo long. I suggest that they would cut it first before serving. All in all, it was still a good experience being able to dine in Cafe Julieta.

The place was really beautiful. The food was great and the service is really good too. All the people was nice... There wasnt much noice from people but theres music playing in the background. No worries, the music is soothing or relaxing. It had a european ambiance. The interior design is elegant, minimal, clean and cozy but still posh. I will definitely go back there. The price point is okay for the food quality. They also do buffets on the weekend and have bundles of food I believe for barkadas.

To be fair their food is good. The place is instagrammable but I think or we think together with the people I was with at that time that the variety of food they served in the buffet setting is so lacking. We were so disappointed that they don't have fruits displayed. Their viands were almost pork cooked in different kinds. They are not totally sensitive of the people who would like to go and eat there. They don't even have vegetable kind of food served, they were all meat. It was so saddening that we expected something good from them because well the place was actually nice. Sad to say to that I think they don't know how to serve buffet correctly, sorry. Tho to be honest I still went home full. Of course how can you waste your money just because somethings lacking. 😄😊 I just wish they could serve fruits and vegetables next time. 🍌🍍🍉

I have been here twice before, the crew were smiling and were ready to serve, the food was exquisite and was the type where you would come back for more. But last night was different. The waitress who served us was sarcastic, there was one plate left to be served, so we asked to please follow it up, then she answered back, "25 to 30 minutes man, ma'am." It was like she was telling us that it hasn't been 30 minutes yet, we knew that, but 4 plates had already been served, and we were just there waiting for it for usbto eat together, so it was more of a gentle reminder, she could have just said that they were still preparing it, but no, she has to point out the time. What a nasty attitude, if you ask me. The food. The food is different now. I ordered NZ tenderloin, medium, mushroom sauce. The moment I poured my mushroom sauce onto my plate, my food felt like it wasn't even heated, because the sauce was colder than your ex-girlfriend. Plus my plate had a crack on it. This looked like an upscale restaurant, the food is not cheap, so why in the world would they allow that to happen? Whatever. I don't think I'm coming back here. Too bad. I used to really love the place.
The Tomahawk steak was really underwhelming. Paid over 7K for the steak alone. The rest of our food was decent. Atmosphere was cozy though. If only they can improve on their food, I'd give a four.

Excellent service. Staff were all nice and responsive to questions. Alam na alam nila ang menu nila. Food served was said to be good for 2 persons but it actually serves more. The atmosphere was perfect.

Casa Julieta was a nice stay, The place was interesting! The deep 10ft and shallow 4ft pool was really cool! There are nice floatees and life jackets. The decorations and lights are cute<3 I had fun here, we spent our Christmas in Dec 26 here for us cousins. I enjoyed swimming in the pool. I rate this a 5-star! For New Year 2022, We'll be spending time here. I'm really happy. This was the best!

Mushroom soup is good. Most of the other foods are also good. The place is an old residential split bungalow which is converted into a restaurant. There is a swimming pool for small kids while the adults eat and drink coffee.

Formerly the Damaso residence on 188 Tulip drive. Spent fond memories inside when it was a private residence. Swimming pool has been maintained and extended. Former bedrooms in the upper floor are converted into function rooms. Gazebo extended and there's outdoor dining. Bright atmosphere and jovial vibes. Good food and great company in this Cafe.

Again, without bias, one of the best places to eat in Davao City. To quote my kids, everything on the menu tastes good... They have a pool, they have function rooms, they have a hotel at the back Casa Julieta, the cakes and pastries in the coffee shop are awesome. The staff are great and reliable. Its a place where you can just sit back and relax knowing you are well taken cared of. So, the next time someone answers "maski asa" when you ask "asa man nimo gusto mu kaon?" Go to Cafe Julieta.
The food is good there. They have choices from steaks to asian dishes. Like seafood laksa. A bit pricey though. And they have cakes also which we really good. I recommend the sans rival cake.

Me and my friend went for lunch. The place is cozy and its clean. I ordered, penne arrabbiata and hers is mac cheese. The taste was too salty and I ask my friend to try it maybe its not that salty for her but it's confirmed. It was too salty, same with her mac cheese.. Too salty...
Not consistent. Loved the food and service one time. Left hungry next time. Service was slow and food was inedible. Too bad. Could have been my favorite breakfast place.
Delicious food and the place is so cozy
Overall ambience is good. chill vibes. Chilli Garlic chicken was the best. Do try. Mac and cheese was not good honestly. Grilled cheese sandwich was okayish.
I love the ambiance of this place and the food was good! Kinda weird to have the pool on the side but nonetheless, quite impressive! Love their carrot cake!
The place is nice to dine in. It took a while before our order was taken, but the staff are quite friendly. The food is fine.
Cool place to eat and relax. Generally food is good, coffee tastes great and the sans rival is superb.
Great food and excellent service!
Recommended for everyone ;-)
The food was great. The place is nice and clean. The service was OK. The place is also ideal for small group gathering.
Lovely staff, delicious food. Kids friendly, You can relax and swim their swimming pool. Thank you 😊
Very nice resto ambiance. The food is average. Their kaldereta is so sweet and too much carrot was added. Friendly staff.
Had my child's Christening here, also had a couple of other meals here and the food is amazing. Really enjoyed it every time we visit.
A very good place for simple and mediocre functions. Good food, good aesthetics, and also have two pools which is one for kiddies and one for adults with a maximum of 10 feet.
Great Food . Great Service.
Great food! Great service! Nice pool for families! They even have function rooms! Overall great customer experience!! 👍🏼👍🏼👍🏼👌🏼🤙🏻🤙🏻👌🏼 …
I had a good experience celebrating my daughter's birthday here. Great food, cozy place, and excellent service.
Overall experience is average. Service is a bit slow and menu selection is limited. However, if only for the ensaymada, its worth the trouble
Slow service food was average. Not sure w Ould go again. Maybe another visit will sway my opinion better
Good food
Highly recommend their private rooms for small get togethers. Food is good, restroom is clean, staff is attentive!

Cafe Tavera remains a solid choice for classic Filipino seafood and comfort food near Torres Street. The Food: Definitely the highlight. Everything we ordered was delicious. The Green Mango with Bagoong and Kinilaw Medley are perfect appetizers to start your meal. Don't miss their famous Dragon Balls (savory meat/seafood balls) - we got the 6-piece serving and they were a hit. The Fried Crab with Salted Egg was rich and flavorful, while the Baked Scallops, Buttered Shrimps, and Calamares were all fresh. We also added the Grilled Pork Liempo for some variety, and it was perfectly charred. The service is okay, though it can be a bit slow when the house is full, so patience is key. The dining area has that classic, cozy Davao ancestral home vibe, but it could use a bit of a refresh to keep up with the newer spots in the city. On-site parking is quite limited. If the small lot is full, you'll have to do roadside parking along Camus or Avanceña Streets. Just be mindful of the "No Parking" signs to avoid towing, especially since the streets are a bit narrow. Pro-Tip for Visitors: They have private air-conditioned rooms perfect for family reunions or business dinners, as well as more intimate corners for couples. Since this is a favorite for local celebrations, be sure to book in advance, as they are often packed on weekends and holidays.

Stepping into Café de Vivré felt like discovering a quiet sanctuary in the middle of a busy day. From the very first sip of my coffee, I could immediately tell: this place takes pride in its beans. The aroma was rich and inviting, and the taste—deep, smooth, and wonderfully nuanced—spoke volumes about the quality of the local beans they use. What makes Café de Vivré truly special is their thoughtful commitment to showcasing local coffee. There's something meaningful about sipping a cup that not only tastes incredible but also supports local growers and reflects the region's unique character. It's more than coffee—it's culture in a cup. The ambiance is warm and welcoming, perfect for both quiet solo moments and good conversations with friends. The staff were genuinely kind, happy to share the story behind their beans and offer recommendations. You can tell they're passionate about what they serve—and it shows. If you're someone who appreciates a good cup of coffee that has both depth and a story behind it, I can't recommend Café de Vivré enough. It's not just a café—it's an experience rooted in local pride and exceptional flavor.

This cafe is proof that a beautiful space cannot make up for complete operational failure. While the decor and ambiance deserve a perfect five stars, every other aspect of our experience was a frustrating disaster. We ordered two drinks and two cakes. After waiting over 40 minutes with no update, we finally asked about our order. That's when they started to scramble. Our drinks arrived about ten minutes later, and both of them were wrong. My friend sipped her hot drink, which was fully covered, and found it was matcha. We did not order matcha. We sent them back. The cakes arrived next, and thankfully they were correct. We ate our entire dessert without our drinks. When we were done, my friend had to go to the counter to follow up yet again. After another long and unmarked wait, the correct drinks finally came. The taste was nothing special. Just okay. A few minutes later, another set of the same cakes was brought to our table. They were so disorganized they did not even know what had been served. Honestly, looking back, we should not have told them. It would have been a small compensation for their total lack of professionalism, but we are not those kinds of people. The final insult was their closing. Our correct drinks were served at 11:05 PM, five minutes after their posted closing time of 11:00 PM. We asked if we could stay to finish, since the delays were their fault and staff were still cleaning. Instead of speaking to us, they began turning the main lights on and off repeatedly. It was a rude and impatient way to treat paying customers. TLDR: Gorgeous to look at, painful to experience. The service is chaotic, the wait is absurd, and the management is clearly in over its head. Do not believe the hype or the vloggers. This cafe is not ready for customers.

When I informed the cashier that we wanted to cancel our orders, she then told me that iced Spanish lattes were no longer available. We've been seeing this place many times but we didn't go cuz they open late before. Just few days ago we saw the signage outside that they serve coffee + bfast and today we decided to go and tried their breakfast. It was good. The food was good and the coffee too. When I arrived there with a friend around noon, there were a couple of stuff I wanted to take note on. One, the staff. When we arrived, they greeted us as soon as we entered, although we were the only customers there so I'm not sure if that would be consistent during peak hours. Second, the service and the food. My friend ordered the cheesy chicken, and I had the spicy hanoy chicken (I was told it was supposed to be honey but it turned out like that due to a misprint in the menu lol) and the cookies and cream frappe. It took around 20 minutes for the food to come out, which is sort of decent in my books considering this isn't a fast food restaurant. The spicy honey chicken was really good, although the rice was a bit dry and the ratio of meat to rice favored the meat more. Additionally, we had a free side dish of kimchi and egg drop soup. I couldn't eat the kimchi because of shrimp allergy but my friend finished both our shares so I'm guessing it was okay, and the egg drop soup was delicious even though I usually prefer it a bit thicker. For those who follow the Seventh Day Adventist diet (no pork, no crustaceans, fish w/o scales etc), I would recommend making sure you know what they're serving with the food since one of the side dishes we had on the plate were squid strips. Also, the food was warm when it came out. Not quite room temperature, but not exactly giving "freshly cooked". The frappe was to die for. That's all I have to say on my drink. Their garden was beautiful and clean, little to no clutter in sight. But there were pretty big dogs in a cage around the back so if you have allergies, or if you're terrified you might wanna avoid going to the corner of their outdoor dining area. They were pretty docile, though. I didn't check their bathrooms out, unfortunately, but the inside area was clean as well and didn't have any weird smells. Even the area outside smelled alright despite being beside a river and a busy road, although I'm not sure how the scent would be at night since we went there around 12 noon. Next, the prices. I'm aware inflation exists and is pretty bad, so I understood the frappe (it was a decent size dw) costing around 150+ and our food was 200+ each, but bro 50 pesos for extra rice? In summary: Do I like the place? Yes. Was the food good? Yes. Would I recommend it for outings and stuff? Maybe a one-time thing, but not enough to go back again and again. Maybe for the frappe heh. Recommend to tourists? Sure, absolutely.

review_text: love the vibe and greenery here. perfect place to read and just chill out. they also have an indoor seating with only few tables if you prefer with AC. matcha is very umami and the cheesecake was superb. does accept cashless and card payments but may be hard if scan to pay bc the signal inside the bldg is kinda wonky.

review_text: We were looking for a café around the area and stumbled by this café. We had no choice because the nearby cafés were already full. place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: A cozy and comforting spot to relax. The cafe has a warm, homey atmosphere that makes you want to stay a little longer. I really enjoyed their cheesecake it was creamy and delicious, though the crust was a bit too sweet for my taste. Still, it's paired nicely with their coffee, making the overall experience worthwhile.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: The best thing about Cafe Prelaya is its cozy vibe. That to me is a 5/5. We stayed at the garden for our early morning breakfast. We ordered pasta, grilled cheese sandwich, and coffee. Coffee was average. The grilled cheese sandwich was tasty. The pasta dishes we had were pretty average too. But do try their caramel pecan cheesecake. Suggestion: maybe add some salads or healthy wraps.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: A lovely place to have cup of coffee. They're open to serve as early as 6 am. Overall a solid 5 out of 5 stars ⭐

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: What I love about this place is its chill vibe. The atmosphere is perfect for relaxation and unwinding. Additionally, the food is absolutely fantastic, especially the pecan cheesecake, which is a delectable treat for the taste buds. Another thing that I adore about this place is their Spanish latte, which is a delightful and flavorful beverage. Moreover, I greatly appreciate the stunning wall art that graces the establishment. The artwork adds a lovely touch and enhances the overall ambiance.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: So far with what we've tried, food was good. The drinks are not bad either. We tried their bestseller pecan cheesecake and matcha latte. Since it was al fresco and that time it drizzled a little bit, we noticed numerous caterpillars on the grounds. They weren't getting in our food and causing annoyance though, so it seemed fine. I dont think they have a bigger indoor area, not sure. Will come back and try other items in their menu next time.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: Cafe Prelaya offers delightful cheesecake and drinks in a charming setting adorned with a cute plant mural. While the food and drinks are delightful, the staff could benefit from additional training in customer service. During my visit, I requested water, and the response was less accommodating than expected, with the staff suggesting I get it outside the door. Considering the lack of other customers, a more attentive approach to customer service could enhance the overall experience and encourage repeat visits.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: Signs of life at 6 a.m. has in itself earned my thumbs-up. Was welcomed by a yawning-under-his-hoodie-yet-wide-eyed barista. Open-air seating makes up most of the area. By half past 7, Hibiscus tonic in hand, I was out the door. Cheesecakes generally, are too much for me but my, oh, my their CARAMEL PECAN cheesecake was a standout. Orange Brew and Plain Cheesecake the following week also did not fail a nod.

review_text: The atmosphere was pleasant. The staff were so friendly and helpful. Contrary to the info that received regarding the being owner so strict. It is a good place to spend time with friends or loosen up with a sip of coffee. During our visit, it drizzled and the staff were quick to assist us in transferring inside and helped us carry our things

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: Loved the quiet and stillness I experienced when I paid this cafe a visit. I tried the Espresso Spirit while I Was there and it was very refreshing. Ordered an Iced Americano for takeout and I noticed that their espresso is light & bright. Will try the hot drinks & desserts next time.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: Not my first time here, but I recently had a strong craving for their caramel pecan cheesecake and let me tell you, they still nailed it! I think they're the only one in the city that serves this, and it was just as rich, nutty, and delicious as I remembered. If I had one wish though... it would be for a bigger slice! It was sooo good but sooo tiny I could cry. 😅 Then again, maybe it's the inflation and I totally get that baking ingredients aren't cheap these days. The café has both indoor and outdoor garden seating, which is a nice option. But do note that the indoor seating is quite cramped...only two tables that are pretty close together. On the plus side, the strong coffee aroma wafting through the café was therapeutic and comforting (especially if you love coffee as much as I do). Only real downside: my cheesecake took several minutes to be served. Not a dealbreaker, but a bit of a wait for something so small, haha. Still a favorite spot for me, definitely worth the visit if you're after a cozy vibe and something sweet.

place_name: Café Prelaya by The Joaquins’ Cheesecakes
review_text: I'm not really into cheesecakes but their cheesecake makes an exception. I love that they are not that sweet and the variant with the roasted pecan topping is divine. Their caffeinated drinks are also not that sweet and goes well with the cheesecake. Easily a recommended cafe in Davao City.

review_text: Their coffee is lit! The flavors are so on point. My partner loved his cold brew and I loved my dirty matcha. It completed our day. No wonder why people notices this coffee shop. The Barista got skills!

December 4, 2025. Arrived at 8:56pm. Been meaning to try to go here just so I can picture the menu for Google reviews. But then they also participated in coffee competitions and crawls so why not? Alfresco area is full. Inside, the table at the corner is taken and the seats occupy the barista entrance space making it like counter seats. My table's lamp is not working but still took my seat. Considering getting from the Davao coffee crawl required drinks but just gone with ₱150 hot Cappuccino for latte art and the art is free as long as available silang magcreate. When the drink is ready, I go to counter and bring it to the table. It wasn't hot which maybe due to Latte art making but I don't mind. Pouring the drink into my cup showed that the hot Cappuccino was 8oz size. Will consider visiting again. Maybe not the food though. Check the ref picture to expect their snacks.

Been a regular since it was a parking lot pop up. Vibes is homey, welcoming, and just friends having good conversation and coffee. Pretty much a glorified tambike space for motorcycle riders both big and small. I usually order hot choco on during nights and my gf's go to is the matcha vol 3. For coffee orders I order cookie dough. Place is very intimate and a good spot if you want a speakeasy coffee place. Not rowdy, not silent, just right. Give it a go, this might be your next go to coffee spot

Please note.. minimum of 10 dogs staying on the hotel for them to assign an attendant looking-out for your dogs overnight. First hand experience, we wanted to pick up our dog around 9:00pm. But there was no one, contacts unreachable. We could hear the dogs barking, I felt they were getting old. No choice, we went back the following morning around 7:30am, there was still no one. So I waited for the staff to arrive, around 8:30am (since their opening time is 9:00am). I asked the staff if they assigned somebody to watch over the dogs during night time. She confirmed that there was a minimum of 10 dogs before they assigned an attendant. Since there were only 4 dogs in the hotel at that time, no one was looking after them at night. Therefore, I was wrong to assume that Pet Hotel is 24/7 with someone attending to the dogs. In case of emergencies, like Earthquake, Fire or something else. There is no safety for the dog. Madat.ogan already there, already toasted in the distance. There is no attendant. In Grooming services, Spa.. I salute them.. clean, smooth work. Only at the hotel. But that's the rules/policy. In short, for those who want a Pet Hotel. Just heads up, ing.ani ilahang system. Hopefully they'll make some positive action regarding this matter.

You know that feeling when you walk into a cafe and instantly feel like you can just kick back? That's exactly how this place is. It's not intimidating or 'too cool' at all—it just has this incredibly welcoming, homey aura from the second you step inside. I tried the Mango Chia Smoothie, and honestly, it's a game-changer. Most places give you that icy, watered-down texture, but this was so rich and creamy. It's the kind of spot where you can actually settle in with a book or your notes and stay a while. Internet: available Mode of payment: cash, e-wallets, cards

It still has that same homey vibe and prices remained reasonable throughout the years. I unfortunately was not able to try their coffee during our recent visit. The tea though is worth it at less than 200 pesos. They will readily give you the wifi passcode upon ordering so plus points for that! They also have small meeting rooms, with consumable packages.

Spanish latte was good but the tiramisu needs improvement. Ambience was great, with warm-color lighting and indoor plants, and dance music in the background. Lots of tables and chairs. Plenty of parking that time. The place was cold initially, but, they would turn off the AC every now and then. Service was okay, however, I noticed that the staff were talking and laughing too loud plus the dance music, so it can get noisy at some point. All in all, it's an okay place to dine.

Today was my first time visiting Coffee at Yellow Hauz. The yellow building catches your eye and the signage is subtle and only on the glass windows. On entering the place was clean with some soft music in the background. I was greeted by the barista and after looking at the menu I decided on the hot Almond Crème Latte and the Cheese Cake Duo. There are plenty of great food and drink options on the menu making it difficult to choose. My latte was bold with slight hints of almond and just the right amount of crème and the cheese cake was delicious without being too rich. Free WiFi for 2 hours and clean CR. An enjoyable experience!

⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Had a wonderful time at Yellow Hauz today during their 19th year anniversary celebration (March 21)! Breakfast was delicious, and what made it extra special was the free coffee all day—such a thoughtful treat for guests. The cozy atmosphere and friendly staff made the experience even better. Truly one of Davao's gems for great coffee and comfort food. Congratulations, Yellow Hauz, on 19 amazing years!
One of the best Cafe stores I've been. Cozy and friendly. They have WiFi and electric sockets. Nice place to do some work.

It's been ages….When coffee shops were still so few, this was one easy place to be…..The interior is different now…. Menu ranges from salads to sandwiches, pasta, rice meals, desserts then down to beverages… After ordering the cashier hands over wifi access vouchers……The grilled cheese sandwich was heavy and cheesy/salty for me….I love the subtlety of the caramel latte…The kani salad was adequate for one person (had to ask for a knife)….Clean place…Good internet connection…Luckily, parking was not full…Eagerly await my next visit….

I recently visited Yellow Hauz, and I must say, the vibe is amazing! The cozy ambiance, and chill atmosphere make it the perfect place to relax. Whether you're there for a quick coffee break or a longer stay. The coffee itself was good – smooth and rich – but there's always room for improvement. Overall, it's a solid choice for your caffeine fix. The variety of drinks available is impressive, and I'm excited to see how they continue to refine their menu.

The Cacao Tea was interesting. First time trying it. It was good. The pastries were okay. Iced Latte was too sweet. There is free wifi connection for 2 hours if you purchase anything. Giving it 4 stars because it has power outlets and wifi. Most shops around the area doesn't have both. Either it has wifi but no power outlet or there is power outlet but no wifi.

This is one of the old coffee shops in the city. I used to hang out with my friends at Yellow Hauz when I was still in college (almost eight years ago)... It's good to know that up to this moment, it is still operating and doing really great. The place has been renovated last year. It's bigger and a lot of things have improved. I will never get tired of ordering their Coffee Cat 😉

This place is so loud! Also, their matcha is soooo bland and watery :( and it's 210??? Update: Kudos to the place for apologizing and thanks for the brownie. Anyway, the matcha could be really improved. I always go to a coffee shop to read like every single day and sometimes twice a day and I just got disappointed with this one. So I hope u'll work on improving this one.

Its location may not be as prominent or accessible as other coffee shops, but Coffee at Yellow Hauz is worth visiting. I love its spacious interiors, several seating options, and work-conducive environment. The shop's cappuccino is according to my liking. I also liked their version of the Clubhouse Sandwich, where they use whole wheat bread. Its best feature? Super fast internet! A quick speed test showed 54Mbps. I like that they're clear on how you can get access -- each of their menu offerings has a corresponding WiFi coupon equivalent.
Just a great cozy atmosphere to drink coffee and eat. The staff is very accommodating and prompt. The coffee and food are always delicious. We just love the Yellow Hauz.

The food and the atmosphere at your establishment are commendable. However, I was deeply disappointed by the behavior of some other customers, which was highly disrespectful. It was particularly troubling that the crew appeared to tolerate such conduct. This is what happened: after I parked my scooter in a designated spot, a customer rudely suggested to the crew that it should be thrown into a canal! This kind of behavior is unacceptable and creates an uncomfortable environment for other patrons. I sincerely hope the crew does not generalize all customers based on these actions, and I strongly urge you to address and discourage such behavior in the future. I would like to continue visiting and working at your establishment, but these experiences are making it difficult, and I can no longer recommend it as a place to eat peacefully.

The person I was with didn't see it coming and it was real funny. Kudos to Yellow Hauz! Awesome service! Place has great vibes. The food and beverages were delightful!

Hubby and I were on a mission to try out cafe's located far from the city proper. Coffee by the way is one of them. We arrived at 2:58pm , they open at 3pm, gladly we were let in though it's just a matter of 2 mins. Upon arriving, we scanned the area as we were the only customer there. We seated at their famous table on the bridge with river below. What we ordered: Hubby got Iced Cappuccino (P150) but he was not happy about it as it was just coffee that was not that strong. Their cappuccino was not that creamy as I had a sip (we exchanged drinks 😅) I ordered Iced Salted Caramel (P165) it was so-so. With a faint salty taste that you cannot really distinguish if you're not that technical when it comes to coffee. It was creamy though and hubby liked it. For food, we ordered Double The Fun (P395) it was just Fries, Hotdog, Nuggets, and Cheese Sticks what I like was the sauce, it was good. Also tried their Quesadilla (P165) did not expect anything but still it was a let down as it's only a tortilla filled with quickmelt eden cheese (it tasted like that) Tried their Aglio Olio (P185) which I was happy. It's got a good level of spiciness that I like. Good amount of olive oil and bacon bits. I just wish they added more garlic and served it with lemon. Nonetheless it was my fave dish so far. Staffs were accommodating and welcoming, a plus 🥹 As for the atmosphere, since we arrived early it was still warm which gradually became cool as it turns late afternoon (4-ish). The sound of river flowing below was calming. There were cute cats too. Worth a visit 👌👌

Coffee by the Way offers a cozy and relaxing ambiance, making it a great place to unwind. The natural surroundings, including grapevines on the perimeter, bamboo and mahogany trees, and a small pool, create a refreshing and tranquil environment. However, there are areas where the café could improve. The menu has limited food and coffee options, which might not cater to more adventurous palates. Additionally, parking can be challenging, especially during busy hours. Restroom facilities also need upgrading to match the inviting atmosphere of the place. Service tends to be slow on Sundays due to the large crowd, so patience is required. Despite these drawbacks, Coffee by the Way is a charming spot for a quiet escape, particularly if you're after a simple, no-frills experience in Davao City.

Coffee By The Way is not just a coffee shop; it's a serene escape into nature, offering an unparalleled coffee experience that seamlessly blends quality brews with a refreshing natural ambiance. This establishment stands out as the epitome of a coffee shop with a nature theme, creating an environment that transcends the typical cafe setting. From the moment you step inside, you are enveloped in a soothing atmosphere adorned with earthy tones, greenery, and wood accents. The décor is thoughtfully curated to emulate the tranquility of nature, providing a welcome break from the hustle and bustle of daily life. The attention to detail is evident in every corner, making it clear that the owners have invested time and effort into cultivating an environment that enhances the overall coffee-drinking experience. We had our coffee by the bridge, beneath is a flowing river with a soothing sound of water ripples. The nature theme extends to the outdoor seating area, providing patrons with the option to enjoy their coffee surrounded by fresh air and greenery. It's the perfect spot for those looking to savor their drink while basking in the beauty of the moonlight. Coffee By The Way stands out as the best coffee shop with a nature theme. It seamlessly combines a tranquil atmosphere inspired by nature with a commitment to serving exceptional coffee, making it a must-visit destination for coffee enthusiasts seeking a unique and refreshing experience.

review_text: A lot of items in the menu are not available. Settled on a lemonade (the only one available from the 4 or 5 listed in the menu) and a pasta (only two choices left from the menu). review_text: I recently visited Coffee Hub, and it quickly became my go-to spot! The atmosphere is cozy and inviting, making it the perfect place to relax or get some work done. The coffee is absolutely amazing—rich, flavorful, and brewed to perfection. Their menu has a wide variety of options, from classic espressos to unique specialty drinks, and each cup is crafted with care. The pastries and snacks were equally delicious, a perfect complement to the coffee. The staff was friendly and welcoming, and the service was excellent. Whether you're looking for a quiet place to unwind or a spot to meet friends, Delicious Food & Amazing Coffee! ☕️ The food and coffee at Coffee Hub are absolutely fantastic! Every dish is flavorful, and the coffee is brewed to perfection. Whether you're here for a meal or just a quick coffee break, you're in for a treat. I'll definitely be coming back for more! Coffee Hub is the place to be. Highly recommended!

Delicious foods..We ordered spam and tapa. Portion servings are okay but food preparation really took a lot of time; which is why, by the time it was served, we were famished and forgot to take pictures 😋😋😋 Staff are also friendly. By the way this place is located within Davao Hub; hence, this is where we prepared (since it's self service 😅) and ate the free continental breakfast ha ha ha. Anyways, I really love the decorations and interior design since it made the place homey, specially in the morning. Ideal place to have some chit chat and just chill 😁 Location is also accessible since it's situated in downtown Davao.

It's quiet, with fast wifi. The space is small with very friendly service. The food is filling and great drinks. Definitely a great place to stay in if you want to study out, I'd love to keep coming back here to study, as well as eat and drink.

The "C" in Coffee Hub stands for cozy. 😙☕️ The place was small and simple. It had a patio for alfresco diners. In total, it can accommodate 20 customers. Moreover, the coffee shop had good choice of furniture; it looked and felt spacious despite its size. The best part: Coffee Hub's comfort room. It was clean and hygienic, complete with bidet, hand soap, and tissue. It earned my vote. I'd say Coffee Hub is the best place for productivity and practicality. It offers coffee and non-caffeine drinks, and meals at reasonable prices (P.S. dirty matcha was good). Every order entitles a customer to 3 hours of wifi connection. Furthermore, it is important to note that the management imposes a 3-hour rule to discourage over-staying. They require customers to make an additional order to extend their stay. Lastly, parking spaces are limited.

Great place for students, working professionals, and groups of friends. Tasty caramel macchiato. High-speed internet connection. Convenient, available 24/7, accessible— location is in downtown, and very accomodating staff. 4/5 stars, carbonara and mocha cake need to improve.

What a huge letdown. A disappointing experience. I went there at around 2 AM. They have no food to serve, absolutely no food at all. As for the drinks, it was so hard to choose something to my liking because they have no decaf, no oat milk, no almond milk, their matcha is not pure matcha, their hot chocolate is powdered (not the authentic cocoa). I ended up ordering a basic americano. Edit: I'm drinking my Americano as I'm typing. This coffee tastes so bad! Ugh!
Well price and very convenient with the long hours they are open. Food and coffee was okay. Atmosphere is a little cramped and the design is a bit busy. Overall nice place.

This place is a great spot for students who need a quiet place to study, especially since it's open 24 hours. The coffee is really good, and the cozy atmosphere makes it easy to focus. I also appreciate that every table has a socket for charging, very convenient! The prices are affordable too, which is perfect for those on a budget. Definitely a nice place to spend some productive time.

Food is okay, but music is kinda loud. This is a caveat you are going to visit here to work/focus. I loved the wifi and the sockets everywhere though. If you will come here to have chitchats with friends or just spend some me time, then this place is okay.
With cozy indoor and outdoor spaces, free wifi, a wide variety of options for drinks, and my favorite: super yummy green tea latte ❤️ they offer some snacks and deserts too!
I love the atmosphere and the staff is accommodating. I also like the snack I ordered. 10/10.

Love their mango frappe. It has right amount of sweetness. They also have free wifi for their customers. Internet speed ranges from 1-4mbps. Atmosphere is pretty decent. Place is cold and they play low volume music.

I've been coming back to Coffee Hub time and time again. Every time, it really is enjoyable. I love the ala carte meals that they have. The sandwiches–both tuna and chicken–are very delicious as well. I have tried many drinks in my numerous visits, but I think my top favorites are the Matcha Oreo Frappe, and the Strawberry Fruit Juice (Or tea, I'm probably wrong). This place is definitely a must try.
Great coffee/drinks, great atmosphere, great internet, very clean bathroom and friendly staff.
Affordable coffee and a freshly brewed coffee beans round the clock plus a comfortable place to kill time.
WIFI OK, coffee delicious , silent Atomosher
One of the cafes in downtown that I recommend since they offer budget-friendly food and beverages that suit their place and services, great for students!
Place is clean , price is over high! A simple tea 150 php..... They need thinking about competitive price as all coffee shop around... I don't recomand
The coffee is great but a little disappointed in the food. Tuna sandwich was mainly salad dressing and barely any tuna.
Went for Breakfast. Really good portions and tasty. Coffee was so good
I love here coffee so delicious and creamy..I love it nice place so clean.
Nice quaint coffee place. They have outdoor sitting also.. will go back
Cozy ambiance, freshly brewed coffee, & online acess. Enhances your productivity.
very expensive but good service

Kind and accommodating.

The food was delicious. I don't order sandwiches often but I enjoyed the sandwiches I did order here. The dessert especially the tiramisu really opened my eyes to the greatness of a well made tiramisu. It was the first and the best tiramisu I have ever had. It made the tiramisus I had after pale in comparison. The other one was delicious as well. I don't like coffee but the coffee here was actually good and complimentary to the dessert. The staff were quite friendly and polite especially compared to the previous place I went to.

Chill place after work or school. Their matcha is really delicious and such flavor. Their place is not too crowded and cramped, just right spacing between tables and chairs. They offer gcash and their staff is nice when I ordered and I asked some things. Unfortunately, they dont have decaf options. I hope it does not get too noisy so we could chill in peace enjoying the cafe experience, and I hope they play more classical and relaxing music because it would fit more in the clean ambiance of the cafe. This is the only branch in Davao so far. Would love to be back next time to try their tiramisus. Great.

Definitely worth the hype. I don't know what original tiramisu supposed to taste like but theirs is so delicious. The matcha tiramisu is also good but too matcha for my liking 😅. Not to mention the banana pudding matcha drink?? Idk the name. Super recommended! The place is quite small, but can cater customer.

Place had shared parking with building tenants. Noise came with the groups of students and office people dining in. Space was clean and new. Mighty pleased with the thick drink and creamy pasta. Short but reasonably-priced menu. I'd like to see an update in choices soon.

Coffee Maybe just opened this weekend so we gave it a try. We got there around noon on Sunday and 4 tables were taken with only one person at each table. They were on their phones and notebooks. We ordered our food and drinks and were able to find a place to sit. We ordered an iced Sea Salt Latte, Vanilla Latte, Hungarian Sausage, Caramelize Spam and Carrot Cake. Our order was ready in 15 minutes and as ordered. I chose not to have rice with the sausage and they offered eggs in place of the rice. We were very happy with our food and drinks. The iced sea salt latte, first time trying this drink, was a pleasant surprise and only a slight taste of salt. The sausage, spam and eggs were all prepared as we hoped and the carrot cake was a great choice to finish off our meal. Service was good, staff friendly, clean bathrooms and no WiFi. It is small inside but comfortable and nicely decorated. Because of the four single people taking up four tables led others that came in to not stay and leave. I'm guessing students even though there was no WiFi. Coffee Maybe is off to a great start.

the place is very cozy, nice ambience, and the moment you enter you can smell the aroma of coffee. The food is great. I recommend you to try their Alfredo Chicken Pasta cuz its so good. It get crowded easily so maybe go there earlier, so you can enjoy the moment and take picturesque photos.

First time here and definitely won't be the last! The matcha with banana pudding was so good, smooth, not too sweet, and surprisingly comforting. The croffles (especially the Biscoff!) were crispy and buttery, made from real croissant dough, super worth it. Also tried the tiramisu, and it did not disappoint. The place is cozy and chill, perfect for catching up with friends or just enjoying me-time. Staff were polite and helpful. A little hidden gem that's worth discovering. If there's one caveat, it would be that not all the staff wore aprons which kind of ticked off the OCD in me. The cashier and another guy at the counter were in plain clothes. I wish they had uniforms or at least aprons for a more cohesive and professional look. Still, the food and drinks made up for it. Will definitely come back to try more.

The matcha tiramisu(latte) is a bomb. It was my first order from this cafe and for sure I will come back to try different blend - the cafe has enough space for group of people too. I wish they can upgrade their system for adding espresso shots for customer's preferrence.

📍 Coffee Maybe, Artiaga St. cor. Bonifacio St., DVO ✅ Open daily from 11 AM to 10 PM ✅ Cozy and artsy vibe ✅ Baristas are friendly and welcoming ✅ Absolutely mouthwatering menu — from coffee, chocolate drinks, pastries, to hearty brunch picks 🩷 Ham and Cheese Croffle - P199 🩷 Iced Signature Chocolate - P180
Parking area is small due to other stores beside this place they had their own customers also. But overall the drinks are great and affordable.

Tried their seasalt latte and biscoff cake during our visit. the cake was okay but didn't complimented our drink. Cafe's ambiance is top tier - giving the aesthetic vibe plus the coffee calm vibes bg music. Had a bit of hard time looking for parking though (parking area outside the building can only hold up to 6-7 cars I guess).
Been here around 3-4 times already! Still my fave café!

Tried chicken alfredo, yum! The chicken that comes with the pasta is yummy too. Tried the biscoff croffle too, and it's also good. The croffle has the crunch you're looking for but for me it kinda lacks something But, it's good naman.

A cafe that's giving me major ig aesthetic vibes! 😉 This cafe is so cozy, even if i only stayed for a sec. I tried the Iced Spanish Latte on the barista's rec, but idk...it was okay at first, then there was a weird aftertaste.
love their food sm! this might be my favorite cafe in davao (also been following them ever since before they had a branch here.)
The cakes are fantastic here, well worth a try.
Ordered Spanish Latte (over ice) and Moist Cake for take out. I love their Spanish Latte, not too sweet which what I like, and their Moist Cake (best seller) tastes heavenly.
Food is good and worth your money. Nice ambience very esthetic. Worthy to visit.

The white chocolate matcha is so good and very promising, except for the amount of ice they put. They put more ice on the cup than the actual drink, so when the ice melts, you won't really taste the flavor of the drink anymore. We even had to request the barista to put less ice when we went the second time just to drink a normal amount of ice and more matcha.
i ordered Iced Americano. It was same as the other elite cafe's and ok sakin. Plus points sakin that time is I tried their black forest tiramisu. Ang sarap!
Ordered an americano and croffle and can'r really say more other than all were delicious. . Although after dining here i did realize the smell of food stuck to my clothes

Great place to tambayyy
Coffee Maybe Holiday drink ✨☕️
Good food, service and atmosphere overall. A bit in the pricy side and the place is a bit small.

Went here for brunch. The place was so cozy and nice. Went there and the place was not too crowded probably depends on day and time. Food was super delicious. Ordered their beef mushroom and it was super delicious. The place was so nice and the comfort room did not disappoint. If you have a car, they have a parking space too.
Went here for 3 days straight haha I really like the food I ordered and wow they have wifi too. It's just weird tho

The menus are delicious, but I'm a little turned off by the sandwich prices, they're expensive and the serving is small. I hope they change the price or make the serving worth the price..it seems like they've skimped on it. Overall the food is delicious, I also tried the chicken with honey and classic spaghetti.

The customer was removed from the seat because they said 6 chairs were "Reserved". while we were seated on the side because there were only 4 of us so we were not allowed to sit. The worst thing is the 6 who reserved, we just finished and they were still not there. Lacked of initiative especially the girl on the counter. tho the food is good but the staff are 5/10. So Embarrassing.

The coffee itself is decent, and the place has a nice ambiance, but the food is unfortunately overpriced for what you get. Portions are noticeably small considering the high prices, which makes it hard to feel satisfied after a meal. The quality of the food is somehow just acceptable and it doesn't justify the cost, especially if you're expecting value for money. This spot might work for a quick coffee, but I wouldn't recommend it if you're looking for quality food. Definitely not going back.

We've been here before, but it was quite busy at the time, so we weren't really able to enjoy the place. This time, we dropped by around 8 AM when there were only a few customers, and it made a huge difference, we got to truly appreciate the ambiance, the spacious layout, and the beautiful interiors. I also discovered a new favorite: their Vietnamese Latte — highly recommended! Along with our drinks, we ordered the Bacon 4 Cheese Sandwich, which turned out to be very generous in portion size and definitely too much for two people. We could barely finish both slices. Lol. Regarding the pricing, some say it's more expensive than Starbucks, but based on our order, we definitely got our money's worth, and then some. The barista was very patient and accommodating. It took us a while to decide, but she remained polite, offered great recommendations, and clearly explained what each blend included. We ended up going with her suggestions and they did not disappoint. Pro tip: The best time to visit is in the morning, when it's still quiet and relaxed. The worst time is late afternoon, as the place tends to get really crowded by then.
Staff are nice and welcoming! Probably the prettiest cafe i've been to here in davao

I don't know about y'all but this place is great. Food may seem expensive but when you get a taste of it, you can say it's worth every peso you spent on it. It's easy to find since it is located just right next to the entrance of the Vista Mall so parking area will not be an issue. The place is a perfect example of what people nowadays call "aesthetic" and their coffee taste so good with a certain bitterness that most coffee lovers what to find in their coffee. If I'm a person who live nearby, I'd probably be here like 2-3 days a week.

Up and running at 7 a.m., this place is accessed from the front of Vista Mall building. Interior design and space is admirable. The menu boasts of choices from all-day breakfast meals to salads, pastas to sandwiches, even pizzas and of course coffee and non-coffee beverages. Seating is also good for groups and solo dining. The Creamy Pesto and Mushroom pasta, Green Apple Cucumber Slush, Mushroom and Chicken Fillet, strong and hot Americano all pricey yet tasty and generous in size. Banana Muffin and Choco Chip Brownies, sadly way too sweet. With its corners and turns, and security guard constantly on his phone, hiding at the side, BE MINDFUL of your belongings.

Coffee Project Mintal is a nice stop in the Mintal area if you want a café with a more polished and comfortable setting. The place feels more designed than a simple coffee stop, so it works well for people who want to sit down, relax a bit, or meet someone in a quieter indoor space. It is a good option for coffee, light food, or a short break while spending time around this part of Davao. The overall atmosphere seems better suited for a slow visit rather than a quick grab-and-go stop.

I wouldn't say that this place is the best, but it's also not the worst. While the place and the aesthetics are something you could post on instagram, the food and coffee however falls short of that vibe. My iced americano taste burnt and my carbonara was mid. Overall, my experience with coffee project is not bad, nor it was memorable to the point that it will be my new caffeine spot.

big portion.... can't even finish the plate, hence the picture....and so delicious, so worth it.....coffee is also good we ordered the chicken parmigiana, and salted egg pasta and vietnamese coffee jelly ambience is really nice, we went here around lunch time though, so waiting time is more than 50 min. but totally worth it.
Nice chill place. The interior is nice, very dim, cozy! I love the lighting the most.

Went there for lunch and there were a lot of vacant tables so i didnt queu. Food was good, coffee was bitter (ofcourse lol). Ambiance was nice and the decorations felt novel. The food price is proportional to the serving so in my opinion it was moderately affordable. It was a good experience. Giving 5 stars since i was satisfied with my dining.
We had breakfast here this morning after our morning run from coastal road. Great place but kinda expensive 😬 Good and clean environment. Has a parking space. Good service ✅

The ambiance and the place is great for hanging out. For productive work too if you can handle the bossa nova playlist. Haven't tried the pizzas yet but the vanilla shakes are mid nothing special. Will update this review once I try more of their food.

Love the vibe of this place! So many options on the menu, it was hard to choose. Yeah, it's a little expensive, but you definitely get what you pay for. They only have a few selections of coffee, though.

Served with bloody chicken. Politely informed the staff that the chicken is not fully cooked. They did get the food and refry it now, it is cooked but it tastes like used oil. No actions made after the second complaint they do not care at all. Your staff did not care at all. Imagine I paid 400 plus for it.
Good food and very cozy. Gives u a "your own world" vibes. Food is good and their beverages may hot or cold are unique. Price is 3 of 5 starwhich is understandable. You are paying for an experience.

Coffee Project is a newly opened Cafe at Vista Mall in Mintal, Davao City. The ambiance is cosy, walls with artistic murals that add warmth and playfulness. It's a self service Cafe. Once you ordered and paid at the counter, a buzzer will be handed to you. You take it to your table and wait until it vibrates and flashes. This means your food is ready for pick up at the hand off counter. Coffee Project offers different kind of pasta, sandwiches, pizzas and the typical Filipino food which is fried chicken with rice. I ordered their Clubhouse Sandwich was humongous. My husband has chosen the Continental Breakfast with huge sausage (which was surprisingly delicious), bacon, fried egg, toasted bread with butter and marmalade, waffles with maple syrup. My verdict: Cosy place, reasonable price and delicious food. Highly recommended!

So far so good, The food here was quite expensive but reasonable. big portion of serving and good for sharing. It is good to meet up your friends or classmate here... Bonus their instagramable place .. nice place.
the thing with this cluttered decor is that they don't clean them after installation. covered in dust. everything else is ok. the sweet potato bake is good.

Not recommended. The food and drinks are overpriced. For example, this cheesecake costs 325 pesos! At first, I thought it was only 225 pesos, but when I checked the receipt, I was shocked by how expensive it was. Especially since the portion was so small. If you're looking for good value, find another coffee shop. This one is seriously overpriced. 🤢🤮
Their cakes and frappe are great, but the staff aren't that great. Better train them again on how to welcome their customers and most importantly...please SMILE! All in all, i enjoyed the food there.

Food is at a pricey side. We ordered pizza for ₱400 and usually it can accommodate 3-4 people but the serving size is most probably good for two. Coffee frappe tasted good and taste equals some of the great local coffee shops here in Davao.

My mom is a picky eater and I brought her here mostly for the ambiance. We ordered fish and chips and arabiata. And what a happy surprise, my mom finished her plate of fish and chips, it was the serving size for 3 ladies. My pasta was excellent too. I initially felt impatient coz it took them 45min to bring our order. But when it arrived, and when I saw the quality of the food, I felt my wait was justified. Just a few things to improve on like having so many nice things being flashed on the promo screen that were not available, like the Harry potter series and even the fruit smoothies, most were not available. Overall, I had a great experience here w/ my mom.

It's a place to relax while enjoying something to eat and drink. The ambiance is so cool. It has a FREE wifi connection once you ordered, BUT it is limited, you CANNOT view YouTube & Spotify. As per their staff, it was blocked. Hehehe...

I am from Croatia, I have travel a lot across Asia and Europe and i am also big coffee lover. This is one of the best coffee shops I ever was in. Beautiful interior. Coffee is amazing and staff is nice and polite. I can only give 5 stars.

Pretty nice spot for coffee and pastries, and other drinks and food. We wanted to have dinner but apparently they were out of rice? In the Philippines with a grocery store attached? Meh. Go for coffee.

Pricepoint a bit expensive, not worth it. Coffee was not that good from all the hype. It was a bit bland, expected to have strong coffee ground taste. The pasta and fish/chips we ordered was also not that good. Edible enough, the fish was not fresh, tastes processed. Food and beverage aside, The place was clean,comfy and nice. Place was instagramable with industrial/dried floral design. Plenty of table to sit. There were plenty of parking space nearby from the Allhome.
Aesthetic vibes pro very pricey. Ordered carbonara for 410 pesos; nothing special about it. Ordered Vietnamese coffe..lami pod..
Place is very aesthetic; feels like you are in a garden wedding. Food is so-so and actually expensive. No dairy-free option. Good to come here for coffee and chilling.
very IG-worthy place. every corner, you can take good pictures. prices are okay.. the drinks are good esp the brewed coffee..

The cafe was supposed to open at 8 am but we were let in at 810 after one of the customers who waiting with us continually asked to be let in already. We waited for OVER AN HOUR for our food. I tasted the chicken with mushroom rice meal when the cafe recently opened and it tasted great, but this time it tasted like a leftover placed in a microwave. Dry, bland .. not acceptable considering we paid a lot for the meal and again we had to wait for over an hour!!!!! The staff need to be retrained or else the business is going down!!!!
The food and drinks don't suit my taste TBH. The ambience of the shop is ok and very instagrammable.

By its visuals alone, Coffee Project in Vista Mall Davao is a must visit! I love the nature-inspired interiors that make every plantito / plantita giggling in sheer delight. We visited the coffee shop on its opening day, and so the queue is understandably long. We'll definitely return one of these days to try out their coffee and dishes.
Cozy place to dine in and work at. The food and drinks are fine, just like most cafes.
so cozy
Great place to meet up with friends, great and varieties of food to choose from, spacious and well mannered staff, must try their sardines & cheese pandesal
Was disappointed in the foods I ordered, the club sandwich had no chicken, no bacon, it was just a regular ham sandwich, the lettuce was not washed on the salad, not worth it, will not eat here again
Very kind workers, free wifi, charging slots scattered every table, good for online classes, work, etc. fast service good quality food/drinks
Highly Recommendable! The place is so cozy and worth to enjoy. Bring your friends and people who are close to your heart.

Very overpriced. One meal costs around 400 and the serving is so small. We used to dine here before but the servings got significantly smaller and the prices are increasing. Safe to say im never going back

No one even bothered to clean the table. Lots of customers but short staffed. Overly hyped. Food was just ok. Nothing really special. Well perhaps just go for the sake of aesthetics, that's what you're paying for anyway. 🤷 …
Drinks are fine. Don't order the rice meals. Creamy chicken is bland. Sisig is all fats. Beef, Bbq and especially the salmon - SO SALTY. Not comparable to Tagaytay branch.
Nice place to have coffee and unwind this place is inside Vista Mall if you got time check it out.

As a coffee enthusiast, I was thrilled to discover Coffee Project, located in Vistamall, Davao City. The ambiance of the coffee shop is simply stunning, with its spacious and well-designed interior that feels like a lush garden. The abundance of natural light and greenery creates a peaceful and calming environment that's perfect for enjoying a cup of coffee or working on your laptop. The coffee at Coffee Project is nothing short of exceptional. The beans are expertly roasted, resulting in a perfectly balanced brew with no unpleasant acidity. You can tell that the baristas take great care in crafting each cup of coffee, ensuring that every customer is satisfied with their drink. But Coffee Project is more than just a coffee shop; it's an experience. Whether you're meeting friends, working remotely, or simply taking a break, the atmosphere of the shop elevates your coffee-drinking experience to new heights. For coffee lovers who appreciate excellent coffee and a beautiful, calming environment, Coffee Project in Vistamall, Davao City, is a must-visit. So, come and indulge in a cup of coffee that will leave you craving for more.

Definitely worth checking out if you're in Mintal.

EDIT: I feel like I made a very lazy review that is ultimately unhelpful, but I'll try my best not to be that guy. Since the owner replied, here is an updated, hopefully much more detailed review. Cake is commercial. The fact that the cake was baked by your mother makes it, in my opinion, worse. Because you can't really fire your mother, or give her feedback about her cake without affecting your relationship. You might want to consider getting another supplier for your cake, because improvement for a young cafe is crucial. To be clear: the cake is okay, it's not bad. Some commercial cakes are not bad. Honestly, I thought you bought your cakes from SNR, which offers the same level of taste and consistency. But there is room for improvement, and there are so many suppliers for cakes that are better. But I guess doing something with your mom is also good, but there's that catch you have to embrace. I suppose what you can do is advertise the cake to be baked by your mother, so that it becomes more alluring and people are more likely to be forgiving. "Coffee was stale." I think stale was the incorrect word. I would say that the coffee was under-extracted. Not enough of the espesso flavor made it into the cup because of either two things: 1) the mug you used makes it very hard to measure and see where your milk levels should be. Honeslty the milk wasn't bad, it's just that the froth was too a half-inch too thick. So I would probably even consider using smaller mugs that make it easier for your barrista to see measurements, rather than stick with aesthetic mugs that ruin the coffee. 2) The machine you use is not commercial grade, which may be a problem in performing especially with high-volume orders. Unforunately I was not able to see what your machine was, so I'm not entirely sure about this, but it certainly feels and tastes that way. I would highly recommend auditing your coffee with a professional barrista so they can give you that consistency in every mug. Now I hope this review is helpful. I will definitely come back to see if there are any improvements!

A cozy little cat cafe tucked away on the second floor above a row of carinderias. During our visit, we met four adult exotic Persian cats and one kitten. The cats looked healthy and had their own enclosed litter area, although one male cat kept bothering two others, who seemed a bit stressed. I hope the cafe prioritizes neutering their cats and considers adopting rescued Puspins in the future. The cafe also has board games to borrow and pixel bricks for sale, making it a nice place to hang out. It can get quite noisy when the cafe is busy, so it may not be ideal if you're looking for a quiet workspace. We only tried the hot coffee and hotdog sandwich with fries, and both were good. It would be great to see non-dairy milk options added to the menu. My only suggestion is for the staff to be a bit stricter about how guests interact with the cats. Some visitors kept following and carrying them, so clearer guidelines on respectful handling would help ensure the cats' welfare while keeping the experience enjoyable for everyone.

was the best restaurant and coffee shop in toril, in my opinion. Coffee is delicious and so WAS the beef rendang, the last time i had it they're now using a lower grade/cut of meat, tougher, more chewy, less flavorful. Now 86(no more, sadly) was once the best experience you can have in toril at the moment for a really nice chill place to relax. Pretty quiet and peaceful. Oh, the music just started; I definitely preferred the quiet to this, but at least it's not blaring and distorted. *UPDATE* music is now always on too loud now, when i've been there, which has lowered my personal score for that. the place was nice when it felt like a chill escape, now just another noisy place, loud and obnoxious enough that i either HAVE TO use my bluetooth earphones to drown it out, or just leave, or not enter at all :-( food, here's my review of the whole menu. BURGERS, are ok, good by local standards, but there's something cloying(disgustingly sweet) i taste when eating the burgers which i can't figure out. like eating cake, or cake with frosting, while having a burger, even when i asked for no sweet sauces on mine. BEEF RENDANG, good, and probably the best dish for my taste in Toril, at the moment. *UPDATE #2* the beef is now another cut, a cheaper more low quality cut full of gristle and bone and fragments. lowered the food score one star :-( CHICKEN BIRYANI flavors are good, but the chicken, for my taste is very dry, not a good thing for such a lean meat like chicken. dry meat seems to be acceptable here tho, so maybe you'll be ok with it if you actually like to eat dry meat. other things to note as of late. there's now a poop smell when sitting outside, and seating is nearly all outside. even if u move around, you'll still smell it. no idea what's the source of this smell, and likely not the fault of the cafe, but not a pleasant thing when ur eating or having a coffee, or whatever. and, getting insect bites in the evening. again, not the fault of the place, so not dinging the place for it, but it is what it is. *UPDATE #2* There's a likelihood you will be breathing in and smelling cigarette smoke while trying to enjoy your meal, or coffee/drinks.

place_name: Dunkin' Donuts- C. P. Garcia Highway
review_text: Tried this newly opened Dunkin' branch near the airport. No issues with the food...the donuts are what you'd expect from Dunkin', consistent and okay. The place itself is also fine and aesthetic. However, the CUSTOMER SERVICE needs serious improvement. The staff were not very welcoming and had nonchalant expressions(parang ang lalaki ng problema sa buhay), which made the experience feel cold. There also seems to be confusion with the queue system. Since there are two entrances (one facing the airport and one facing Shell), customers don't know where the line starts or ends...there are no clear signages. I've actually raised this concern to the staff during two separate visits last Drcember 2025 and January 2026, but unfortunately, the response felt dismissive and unaccommodating. After this, I didn't visit again. It's a bit disappointing, especially for a newly opened branch in a high-traffic area where many travelers and tourists will pass through. Hopefully, management can address the service and organization soon.

went there during their soft opening. the place was huge, with a lot of seats available—good for solo diners, families, and groups. they have free wifi (i think it's unlimited), plenty of sockets, and a parking lot. the staff were very accommodating. banana muffin – 7/10 a bit dry inside, but still good. i love how the café's logo is printed as a chocolate topping. matcha latte (oat) – 9/10 nutty, mid-bold, with a slight bitter aftertaste. oreo milkshake – 9/10 really good and a big serving. usda beef salpicao – 9/10 good for about 2 servings. the beef was soft and had a rich, not-too-sour flavor. however, i think the price didn't quite match the serving size. overall, it's a nice place to hang out or study because of the space, wifi, and outlets. it would be even better if they added more rice meals like chicken dishes or some pica-pica, since their food choices are currently limited aside from pastries.

Entering this place commands a different climate. Not only is it new but the aura is warm and light. Even the open space at the side is charming. Parked in the garage. Took home some pasta and it was delicious as well. Would absolutely pop in again.

Went there around 8 PM, it wasn't too crowded, and the waiting time for the order was alright. However, the fries weren't that good. The place is really nice and aesthetic. The coffee is 100% arabic beans…it keeps you awake 💯
